entries.title: The Empire Strikes Back, 1980 - ★★★
entries.review:
Idk man, didn’t really live up to the hype. 
 A whole bunch of fighting scenes that were, in retrospect, not that entertaining lol but I’m sure it was at the time. I guess now I’m just used to the fighting scenes of today’s Star Wars universe where the choreography is so well done. The new era makes the fighting here seem robotic.
 Not much else to say outside of that, besides the big reveal that would be impossible not to know about at this point in culture. Some great writing in here too!
 Solid

entries.title: Mother Mary, 2026 - ★★★
entries.review:
A ton of dialogue that felt more like a play than a movie, but both Michaela and Anne were in their bag. 
 More of a suspense than a horror movie tbh and the suspense is definitely… suspenseful. Don’t know if it laddered up to anything though as kept expecting something to show up or to simply happen… and it didn’t haha. 
 Beautiful shots throughout the film though. There are gonna be so many stills that will live from this movie. 
 Also, Anne Hathaway surprisingly does a pretty solid Beyoncé impersonation. Who knew? What can’t this woman do!

entries.title: Star Wars, 1977 - ★★★★★
entries.review:
After seeing just bits and pieces of this one over the years, I can attest that this is pretty epic and magnificent. I now get what the people say about the franchise. There’s  something about this story that feels bigger than just Star Wars. It feels very human and grand like the avatar movies do to me. 
 Watched this immediately after watching both seasons of Andor and Rogue one and honestly, this viewing experience is pretty peak because the way they go from Andor’s timeline… directly into Rogue one… directly into a movie made 50 years ago…. Is insanely smooth. 
 George Lucas, you’re a…

entries.title: The Christophers, 2025 - ★★★
entries.review:
Funny at times but kinda slow. Was cool to see a different side of the art world and the business side of it. 
 Also, Michaela Coel serves face for 140 mins straight so I’m not mad at it at all.

entries.title: Wasteman, 2025 - ★★★★½
entries.review:
Great performances from David and Taylor. They have amazing on screen chemistry and played off each other very nicely. 
 The whole movie keeps you in suspense throughout while subtly (and not so subtly) giving you a peek behind the curtain and commentary on the prison system. Found it interesting the slight differences between how the system is depicted in the UK vs. the US. 
 Regardless, I found myself relating with David Jonsson’s character a lot… yeahhhhhh I’m not build for this bro get me tf outta here 🤣. 
 Was cool to see them in person and hear their pov’s of making the film. Shoutout…

entries.title: Marty Supreme, 2025 - ★★★★★
entries.review:
The hype for this movie has been astronomical and it still exceeds expectations I’m afraid.
 Every chapter of this wild ride feels fully baked and like  is it’s own world that perfectly ladders up to the overall arc of the story. Timothee is magnetic for 2.5 hours straight (of course at this point) and there’s just no way you’re not rooting for him the entire time. Marty’s sheer disregard for everything (and everyone) he touches in the name of his dream is so absurd that it becomes admirable. 
 Even with that, Gwyeneth Paltrow might just have my favorite performance. Odessa A’Zion also did…

entries.title: Babylon, 2022 - ★★★★★
entries.review:
Babylon just gets better every time I watch it. It hits even harder with the current state of Hollywood in a massive moment of disruption with the introduction of AI, and very recently seeing the immediate impact of OpenAI’s latesf release, Sora 2. 
 A constant reminder of why I love movies and the role they play within in our culture and overall human experience.

entries.title: Twinless, 2025 - ★★★★ (contains spoilers)
entries.review:
This review may contain spoilers. 
 I had a lot of fun watching this one. So much if my respect goes to James Sweeney (who I hadn't heard of before this movie), but to find out after the fact that he was not just the lead actor, but also the director AND the producer... an insane display of talent.
 Twinless has tons of funny moments that feel so authentic and genuine. The way they balance humor with some of the harder to accept human emotions like grief, inadequacy, deceit and forgiveness, is such a fantastic display of nuanced writing. The way I was able to relate with pretty much every…

entries.title: HIM, 2025 - ★½ (contains spoilers)
entries.review:
This review may contain spoilers. 
 I had a feeling that this wouldn't be great simply from the way that they were marketing the film with Jordan Peele's name all over it despite him just being the producer... but I didn't expect it to be THIS bad. 
 Let me start by saying that there were some bright spots here that made the movie not a complete waste of time. It's visually appealing (desert was perfect for this), the soundtrack kept things entertaining throughout, and there are a couple of solid acting performances. I'm a fan of Tyriq Weathers (ever since that Atlanta episode) and feel that…

entries.title: The Long Walk, 2025 - ★★
entries.review:
This was a long walk for a wet, soggy, sweaty, bloody ham sandwich. 
 With too many plot holes to count, they really should’ve left this one as a book. Some solid moments here or there, but I left the theater massively underwhelmed and disappointed. 
 This needed a lot more up front and character building to be able to pay off some of the choices made. There wasn’t much so I just kept asking myself… “why would you even do that???”
 David Johnson did his thing and I’m a fan of his in general. The British to southern accent was throwing me off though ngl

entries.title: Caught Stealing, 2025 - ★★★½
entries.review:
Imagine if Uncut Gems and Anora had a baby. You’d get Caught Stealing.
 First act was ehhh but things got a lot better over the course of the movie. It definitely fits the sexy aesthetic that it’s marketed as. Beautifully shot and well casted. Austin Butler did his thing but Matt Smith as Ross still the show. 
 Solid!

entries.title: Freakier Friday, 2025 - ★★★½
entries.review:
Nice throwback with a new twist. Love that they didn’t just copy and paste. I kinda got confused a few times with it being four swaps instead of two, but this movie was filled with some high quality call backs that paid homage to the OG. 
 Also “take me away” might just be the best TV-movie hit song from the early Disney channel era.

entries.title: The Brutalist, 2024 - ★★★★
entries.review:
A very visually and sonically appealing movie. Bring back the mid-movie intermission!
 Loved Brody in this and every cast member acted their asses off, but honestly, Guy Pearce took the cake for me. He hasn’t lost a step. In fact, he’s gained more steps than tap dancer. 
 Only thing keeping me from making this a 4.5 or 5 stars is that the second half doesn’t fully live up to the first half for me. 
 Well worth the 3.5 (actually 4) hours.

entries.title: A Complete Unknown, 2024 - ★★★★½
entries.review:
Cool guy Bob Dylan doing cool guy things. I’m officially a fan. 
 Timmy C was the perfect cast for this role. Wouldn’t be surprised if he takes home an Oscar for it

entries.title: Nickel Boys, 2024 - ★★★★★
entries.review:
I’ve been out of the theater for about 25 mins now and I still don’t know exactly what to think or how to feel. I haven’t felt like this after a movie in quite some time. 
 The book has already been purchased and a second viewing is in the works. 
 Talk about a buzzer beater for movie of the year…
 Must watch

entries.title: Dìdi (弟弟), 2024 - ★★★★½
entries.review:
If nostalgia was a movie..
 Growing up during this time and balancing being a teen/pre-teen with what we now know is technology that would, in very short order, change the world forever… is a trip and a half. Didn’t even realize that I was living in the very last days of an era while simultaneously living in the very first days of a brand new one. 
 This movie does a great job at showing the joys and conflicts that came with that and I don’t think I’ve seen a movie (besides a social network) that does it this well and so relatable. 
 This is one of my new favorites

entries.title: Alien: Romulus, 2024 - ★★★★½
entries.review:
New and refreshing. Very layered film that touches a lot of topics relatable to modern times and where society may be heading in the near future with AI. 
 Acting performances were top notch. David Jonsson is a rising star and I’ll probably watch any movie or show with him in it from now on. 
 A+ movie viewing experience

entries.review:

 However, Hugh Jackman is STILL in a league of his own when it comes to this acting shit
